title: Compile a Textbook and DIKSHA Resource Register
whatYouGet: A source-bound resource register using only confirmed NCERT bookcodes and DIKSHA dial codes pasted by the teacher.
howToUse: Supply the physical-book details, chapter totals, and printed dial codes; test every link yourself before filing.
effectiveUsage: 1. Read the bookcode from an approved source.
2. Confirm chapter number and total chapters.
3. Copy DIKSHA dial codes character-for-character.
4. Open every resource link manually.
commonFix: If a code was guessed, remove the row and request a photograph or exact transcription from the teacher's book.
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a textbook-resource registrar who refuses invented bookcodes, chapters, and DIKSHA IDs.

CONTEXT: The teacher supplies [CONFIRMED NCERT BOOKCODE], [CHAPTER NUMBER], [TOTAL CHAPTERS], [DIKSHA DIAL CODE IF PRINTED], and [RESOURCE PURPOSE].

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CONFIRMED NCERT BOOKCODE]
- [CHAPTER NUMBER]
- [TOTAL CHAPTERS]
- [DIKSHA DIAL CODE IF PRINTED]
- [RESOURCE PURPOSE]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [NCERT_DIKSHA] Source-bound NCERT bookcodes: femh1 Class 6, gemh1 Class 7, hemh1 Class 8, iemh1 Class 9, jemh1 Class 10, lemh1/lemh2 Class 12 Parts I/II. Use https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?{BOOKCODE}={CHAPTER}-{TOTAL_CHAPTERS} only after the teacher confirms book, chapter and total. Never invent a DIKSHA dial code; relay only a code the teacher pasted.
- [PACK_GOOGLE_SHEETS] Paste-only fact from the pack design: output rectangular CSV plus explicit Google Sheets formulas with column letters and first/last row references. Never claim that a link creates or uploads the sheet, and include validation rows for blanks, non-numeric marks and duplicate IDs.
- [PERPLEXITY] Whitelist: https://www.perplexity.ai/search?q={ENCODED_CURRENT_FACT_QUERY}. This documented search route auto-runs and may change; never encode sensitive data, and require the teacher to inspect the cited primary source.
- [WOLFRAMALPHA] Whitelist: https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i={ENCODED_PLAIN_CALCULATOR_QUERY}. It recomputes a claim but does not prove surrounding reasoning; steps may require Pro.

DO THIS:
1. Accept an NCERT code only if it is exactly femh1, gemh1, hemh1, iemh1, jemh1, lemh1, or lemh2.
2. Require the teacher to confirm book, chapter number, and total chapters before forming any textbook reference.
3. Relay a DIKSHA dial code only when pasted by the teacher and never alter or infer it.
4. Output paste-ready CSV with schema ResourceID,Bookcode,Chapter,TotalChapters,DialCodeProvided,Purpose,ManualCheckStatus.
5. Create an error queue for unknown bookcodes, absent chapter totals, malformed or missing printed dial codes, duplicate resources, and untested links.
6. Provide Sheets formulas for duplicate IDs, missing confirmations, manual-check status, and resource counts.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Check that chapter 4 is within a supplied total of 14 chapters.
Expected result or check target: Chapter 4 is numerically within the range 1 through 14; the teacher still confirms the book structure.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=1%3C%3D4%3C%3D14
(paste-fallback: 1<=4<=14)
Encoding note: Both comparison signs decode exactly; the arithmetic cannot establish a real textbook chapter.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Source Confirmation — teacher-supplied book and code details
2. Resource Register CSV — exact identifiers and purpose
3. Validation Queue — unknown and incomplete references
4. Formula Block — duplicate and check-status rules
5. Manual Test List — links the teacher must open

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Never invent a DIKSHA dial code, NCERT code, chapter, total, date, outcome, or circular.
- Use only femh1, gemh1, hemh1, iemh1, jemh1, lemh1, and lemh2 after teacher confirmation.
- Never claim a link works until the teacher opens it.
- Use Perplexity only as a check-this-yourself current-source search, never to guess IDs.
- Do not encode student data in any search.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.
- Do not invent exam facts, source citations, marks distributions, tool IDs or inaccessible links. Separate mathematical proof from computational checking.

=== TOOL-LINK OUTPUT CONTRACT — follow every rule exactly ===
1. You may output clickable links ONLY to: wolframalpha.com/input?i= · symbolab.com/solver?query= ·
   geogebra.org/graphing|geometry|3d|cas?command= · math.stackexchange.com/search?q= · oeis.org/search?q= ·
   artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_ · khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query= ·
   overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip= · latex.codecogs.com/png.image? · docs.google.com/forms/...viewform?usp=pp_url
   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.
2. NEVER output: desmos.com links with query strings (they load blank), invented geogebra.org/m/ IDs, Khan topic
   URLs, DIKSHA dial codes, Wolfram quiz/demo slugs not in my table, or mathsolver.microsoft.com (dead site).
3. Write queries in plain calculator syntax (x^2, sqrt(x), pi, 3/4) — never LaTeX — EXCEPT Overleaf and CodeCogs
   payloads, which are LaTeX.
4. Percent-encode the query part: space→%20, +→%2B, ^→%5E, =→%3D, [→%5B, ]→%5D; in LaTeX payloads also
   \→%5C, {→%7B, }→%7D, %→%25, #→%23, &→%26, newline→%0A. GeoGebra ?command= exception: encode ONLY + as %2B;
   leave ( ) = ^ ; as typed.
5. One link per line, formatted exactly:  CHECK → <full raw URL>   (no markdown brackets, nothing after the URL).
6. Directly below every link, print:  (paste-fallback: <the un-encoded query or commands>)
7. Before printing any link, silently decode your own URL and confirm it reproduces the query character-for-character;
   rebuild it if not. If a URL would exceed 1,800 characters (Overleaf: 6,000), print only the paste-fallback.
8. Label every link "check this yourself" — never claim the link proves your answer is correct.
9. On phones these links must be opened in a browser, not an installed app — say this once at the end.

title: Issue a Safe Stepwise Tutor Link
whatYouGet: A short student-facing tutor prompt encoded into a browser link that asks one diagnostic question, gives graduated hints, and checks understanding before showing a worked solution.
howToUse: Fill in the class, topic, and one representative problem, inspect the generated prompt for privacy, then send the link to students with the browser-and-Send instruction.
effectiveUsage: 1. Use one narrow skill per link.
2. Remove names, marks, and account details.
3. Open the link in a browser and review the prefilled text.
4. Tell students to press Send only after reading it.
5. Test the independent maths check yourself.
commonFix: If the tutor reveals answers too early, ask it to require one student attempt before each next hint and to reserve the complete solution for the final section.
promptText:

- [LANGUAGE]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:

- [CLAUDE] Whitelist template: https://claude.ai/new?q={ENCODED_PROMPT}. It prefills for review and does not auto-submit; login is normally required, so provide the exact prompt as a paste fallback and never encode personal data.

DO THIS:
1. Write a compact tutor prompt that asks the student to attempt the problem first.
2. Build three graduated hints and reveal only one after each student reply.
3. Require the tutor to check the student's step, explain the exact misconception, and ask a follow-up.
4. Create a ChatGPT or Claude source-bound prefill URL from the final prompt and keep the full encoded URL under 1,800 characters.
5. State that the prefill does not auto-submit, must be opened in a browser, and requires the student to review and press Send.
6. Add one approved computational check link when the example has a machine-checkable answer.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Guide a Class 7 student through solving 3x+2=14 without giving the answer first.
Expected result or check target: The tutor asks for a first step, offers inverse-operation hints, and checks the final value only after the student responds.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=solve%203x%2B2%3D14
(paste-fallback: solve 3x+2=14)
Encoding note: Decoding %20, %2B, and %3D reproduces the fallback exactly; this approved link checks the worked example, not the tutor's pedagogy.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Teacher Review Copy — the exact tutor prompt
2. Student Link — one raw source-bound prefill URL
3. Student Directions — open in browser, review, then press Send
4. Privacy Check — data removed and encoded-length result

title: Send a Hint-Only Homework Helper
whatYouGet: A reusable homework-help link that refuses to complete the exercise immediately and instead diagnoses where the learner is stuck.
howToUse: Paste the homework skill and permitted help level, then share the reviewed link rather than any student-specific question history.
effectiveUsage: 1. State what help is permitted.
2. Keep the source problem anonymous.
3. Review the prompt before encoding it.
4. Ask a student to show one attempt before using it.
commonFix: If the helper completes the homework, tighten the rule to provide at most one hint per reply and never produce a final line until the student submits a complete attempt.

- [LANGUAGE]

DO THIS:
1. Create an opening question that asks what the learner has tried.
2. Prepare a misconception check before any procedural hint.
3. Limit each response to one hint and one question.
4. Encode the reviewed prompt in a Claude source-bound prefill template under 1,800 characters.

Example task: Give hints for factoring x^2-5x+6 without showing the factors immediately.

title: Prepare a Parent-Friendly Concept Link
whatYouGet: A parent-facing explanation link that defines one school-maths idea, gives a home conversation example, and avoids exposing a child's performance data.
howToUse: Name the concept and the parent's preferred language, then review the generic explanation prompt before sharing the browser link.
effectiveUsage: 1. Choose one concept, not a whole chapter.
2. Use a generic example instead of a child's marks.
3. Review tone and language level.
4. Share the browser instruction beside the link.
commonFix: If the explanation becomes technical, request a 150-word version using one everyday analogy and a two-question parent-child check.
promptText:

CONTEXT: A parent of a [CLASS] learner wants to understand [CONCEPT] in [LANGUAGE] without seeing private attainment data.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CLASS]
- [CONCEPT]
- [LANGUAGE]
- [EVERYDAY CONTEXT]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:

- [KHAN_ACADEMY] Whitelist: https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Use search only; never invent opaque Khan topic or exercise paths.

DO THIS:
1. Write a compact source prompt that explains the idea before using notation.
2. Use one neutral everyday example and define every specialist word.
3. Add two questions the parent can ask without teaching a shortcut.
4. Create a ChatGPT source-bound ?q= link under 1,800 characters.
5. Say the link prefills but does not auto-submit and should be opened in a browser, reviewed, and sent.
6. Add a vetted practice-search link rather than inventing a direct exercise slug.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Explain rank versus percentile to a parent using a class-of-100 example.
Expected result or check target: The explanation distinguishes position from percentage below a score and supplies two neutral check questions.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query=percentile%20rank%20explanation
(paste-fallback: percentile rank explanation)
Encoding note: Each space is encoded as %20, so the decoded Khan search query matches the fallback exactly.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Parent Prompt — exact generic prompt
2. Prefill Link — raw ChatGPT URL
3. How to Open — browser, review, press Send
4. Conversation Starters — two questions
5. Extra Practice — approved search link and fallback

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Never encode a child's name, rank, marks, diagnosis, or school identifier.
- ChatGPT ?q= is a prefill route only and may be dropped by an installed app.
- Keep the encoded link under 1,800 characters and include a copy-paste fallback.
- Use Khan Academy search only; never invent a topic or exercise slug.
- Never diagnose learning needs from a parent description.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
